id_form_note: provider_id_form is the value a provider default would actually carry, and is what the guard compares against. reported_display_name is what the executor states in prose. These differ in shape, and a guard comparing a display name against settings.CLAUDE_MODEL would never fire regardless of its contents.
not_a_verification: This file records self-reports. It establishes nothing about which model in fact produced any artifact, and must not be cited as establishing it. The pattern is the one ABS-0004 applies to standing authority: the claim, its date, and what it covers are recorded and legible; the claim itself is not verified, and no arrangement of records here could verify it. What the file provides is that a reviewer-slot default can be checked against a maintained list rather than against one literal frozen at the moment a single session happened to be observed.
purpose: Identities that have acted as drafting executor in AI-Lab sessions, so the reviewer-slot default can be checked against all of them rather than against one hardcoded literal. Under ABS-0004 C3 an invocation cannot adjudicate a claim whose evidence ancestry contains an invocation by an equivalent executor identity; configuring the reviewer slot to a drafting executor's identity would collapse reviewer and author.
unclosed_gap: Conversational drafting produces no InvocationRecord, so no record establishes who drafted any artifact. A machine check of C3 over ABS-0004 v8 finds no conflict, not because none exists but because the drafting act was never an Invocation. Slice C's one-hop check reads produced_by relations on the target artifact and would also find nothing. This file makes the reviewer-slot guard maintainable; it does not close that gap, and adding an entry here is not the same as capturing a drafting invocation.
